text: MSCI Adopts New Index Exclusion Rules; Strategy and Metaplanet Face Potential Removal MSCI has adopted new rules to exclude non-operating companies from its Global Investable Market Indexes. In an earlier simulation based on May 2026 data, MSCI identified Bitcoin treasury companies Strategy (MSTR) and Metaplanet (3350) as potential removals, while Ethereum treasury company SharpLink (SBET) would be placed on a watchlist. The final list of affected constituents will be published on November 11. The new rules, effective after the November 30 close, will exclude companies that fail an operating-assets test and trigger at least four of five financial exclusion criteria. Existing constituents must fail the screening in both of their two most recent annual filing periods before removal. MSCI will also lift temporary index restrictions on companies previously identified as holding digital assets worth at least 50% of total assets, assessing them under the new methodology instead. — link

text: One of the hardest parts with trading onchain is having to remain permanetly optimistic while sticking to risk management. The only way you can truly ride out runners and capture whole metas is to be so die hard that you see a billion dollar outcomes in your coins. Staying optimistic and looking for the positive in every project is the only way you're going to find diamonds in the rough and subtle differences between larp tech or strong narratives. At the same time, having strong enough risk management which is correlated to: ⁃ Amount of volume/frequency of runners ⁃ Deployers, vamps, bundles ⁃ Your read on the market and accuracy on previous pa ⁃ Sustainability of metas/narratives ⁃ Potential catalysts (positive and negative) Etc Conviction traders will always make for the aesthetic PNLs, however time and time again the roundtrips are crushing to watch. The only method I've really found that works is playing with tiny size 0.25-0.5% of port per trade and building your framework around that sizing until you reach a specific number of trades/win percentage/confidence in own abilities to allow yourself to size up. Most of the time I usually put a timeframe on these conditions such as: <1 week = 0.25% per trade, 1-2 weeks = 0.5%, 2-3 weeks = 1% etc. This needs to be met with a specific amount of screen time each day and assuming you're approaching this like a professional job. Anything less means you're lying to yourself and slowly self destructing through your own discipline. The times I find myself getting most tilted is always due to sizing and dishonesty with my read on the market. Good conditions might arrive but you haven't put in the work prior to justify the sizing of your trades, which are typically met with loose validations/invalidations. Every time I've stuck to this style of framework and been patient, waiting until my read is up to the markets standards, I eventually hit home run trades as I'm not chasing the market, I'm chasing my own accuracy and peak performance. Time and time again I find this being the biggest differentiator in my success when going through old notes and mental models. Your emotions are the enemy and as someone who leans into conviction trading/ball tingle, even a hard coded framework is needed for myself to not drift off course. There's nothing worse than seeing a killer narrative that you're mentally in the position to capture, except you don't have a good source of capital to make that trade worthwhile. Even with how conditions have been, the one thing you need to continually remind yourself is: you can find good trades if you put in the work. Most (including myself) lie about the effort and work they're putting week in week out over a long timeframe. When you show up everyday with perfect practice, it's a matter of time before luck meets you down the road. There's no other secret sauce or AI agent that's going to change this, discipline will always be triumphant no matter how talented you are.
